subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the beautiful female singer from the reference image <Image 1>, and must STRICTLY follow <Image 1>: her face, hairstyle, build, outfit, accessories, proportions and any props must match <Image 1> exactly in every frame, in the same style.
<Image 1> is the reference image establishing both the character and the scene; it is the identity and environment anchor and must be STRICTLY copied 100% — the singer and the studio / performance stage must remain exactly as in <Image 1> in every frame, keeping the same look, same colors, same lighting design, same props and same stage. Do NOT redesign, restyle, or drift from <Image 1>.
<Audio 1> is the actual song to be performed: <Subject 1> sings this song live, her mouth and expressions syncing naturally to the vocals and the rhythm of <Audio 1>.

summary:
[Reference-based generation] <Subject 1>, the beautiful singer from <Image 1>, performs a song on the exact same studio stage of <Image 1>, singing toward the camera with a natural, expressive, cinematic performance — lip-syncing the actual song <Audio 1>, with a smooth, elegant camera move. Single continuous shot. The voice and music are the actual song from <Audio 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - identity and scene STRICTLY locked to <Image 1>: face, hairstyle, build, outfit, accessories, proportions, the studio stage background and the props must not drift in any frame.
<Image 1> (character & scene reference): fully_preserved - the singer and her studio stage are STRICTLY copied 100% as the visual anchor; no redesign, no restyling, no color changes, no proportion changes, no stage changes.
<Audio 1> (actual song): fully_preserved / audio_transfer - the song from <Audio 1> is the actual audio: she sings this exact song, her lips, expressions and body movements syncing to the song's lyrics, melody and rhythm from start to end.

detailed_description:
The target video is in a high-quality, realistic, cinematic music-performance style with studio stage lighting, shallow depth of field and visible film grain.
[Shot 1] A single continuous shot, its duration matching <Audio 1> (the full song) — ONE CONTINUOUS CAMERA MOVE, no cuts, no zoom, no sudden moves; the camera moves slowly, smoothly and steadily throughout, keeping the singer in frame at all times.

CAMERA (elegant, single continuous move): The shot opens on the singer in a medium shot, front-facing, on the stage of <Image 1>. Over the first third of the song the camera slowly pushes in (a gentle dolly forward) toward her, tightening the framing as the song builds and her emotion grows. Through the middle third, the camera holds a closer medium framing while performing a very slow, subtle lateral drift or a slight arc around her (a gentle truck left or right), revealing a little more of the stage depth behind her. In the final third, the camera slowly pulls back (a gentle dolly out), widening back out to a fuller shot of her on stage as the song resolves, ending on a settled, slightly wider framing as the final note lands. The entire move is one smooth, continuous, elegant motion — never fast, never jittery, never passing in front of the singer, never cutting, never changing her identity or her stage.

The beautiful singer from <Image 1> stands on the same studio stage of <Image 1>, facing the camera, positioned as in <Image 1>, and stays on stage and in frame the entire time.

SINGING & LIP-SYNC (hard constraint): She sings the actual song from <Audio 1> live, mouth and lips syncing naturally and accurately to the vocals and lyrics; her breathing, phrasing and expressions follow the song's melody and emotional arc from the first note to the last.

EXPRESSION ARC: The shot follows the emotional arc of the song — she starts in a focused, composed singing expression, then as the song builds she becomes more emotionally expressive: eyes conveying the feeling, a growing connection with the camera, subtle changes of expression matching the song's mood (soft and tender, then more powerful or joyful at the peak), ending on a natural, held, satisfied expression as the final note lands.

ACTIONS (natural singing performance, alive not stiff): Throughout the shot she performs naturally while facing the camera — subtle head tilts and nods to the beat, a raised hand or open palm gesturing to the lyrics, a slight sway or weight shift with the music, a hand lifting toward her chest during an emotional phrase, small, smooth, professional singer's movements. All motions are natural, musical and on-brand — never exaggerated, never stiff, never still-photo frozen, never changing her proportions, her outfit or her stage; she never turns away from the camera for more than a brief moment.

Micro-motion throughout so she never freezes or looks like a still photo: gentle breathing, slow blinks, small head tilts, the natural singing gestures, the emotional arc, then a calm, satisfied end. She stays grounded on stage and in frame the whole time.
The face, hairstyle, outfit, proportions, the stage and the entire scene must STRICTLY remain 100% consistent with <Image 1> in every frame — no facial morphing, no identity drift, no scene changes, no outfit changes, no proportion changes, no extra limbs or fingers.

overall_soundscape:
The actual song <Audio 1> playing in full — the singer's live vocal, melody and instrumental accompaniment — mixed with a subtle live-performance room tone and the natural reverb of the studio stage.

non_diegetic_music:
The song itself from <Audio 1> is the primary music — no additional score; any underscore stays minimal and only supports the song's own arrangement.
